clue.text: Monarch unattended by day is wise man

blocks.note: a king is a monarch
going solo means acting alone, unattended
Mon is the short form of Monday, a day; 'by' places it next

explanation.surface: A king going about without attendants during the day is shown to be wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical King Solomon is proverbial for wisdom, so his name is used for any sage.

clue.text: Working Greek hopes staff refrain from using drugs?

indicators.note: letters set working are put into action and moved about into a new order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek employer hopes the workforce will steer clear of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: grass is slang for cannabis, so the lawn-sign warning is read as advice to avoid drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The park notice is reinterpreted with grass in its slang sense of cannabis, a whimsical cryptic reading.

clue.text: Identifies pins

blocks.note: first meaning: to pin down or identify precisely, as a detective does a culprit
second meaning: slender metal spikes used for fastening

explanation.walkthrough: Both words can be verbs, but the second meaning is the plural noun for metal fasteners.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to pinpoint or catch someone; the noun is the hardware hammered into wood.

clue.text: Hospital admits mistake over type of ham

indicators.note: to admit is to let someone in, as a hospital takes in a patient, so one part goes inside

blocks.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
to err is to make a mistake
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A hospital confesses to an error involving the ham it served.
explanation.definitionFit: Serrano is a dry-cured Spanish ham, so it is one particular kind.

clue.text: Lively young woman's coffee-drinking diet regularly used

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one is kept
a drink goes inside the drinker, so one part swallows another

blocks.note: a latte is a milky coffee
first and third letters

explanation.surface: A lively young woman sips coffee as part of a diet she sticks to.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a boisterous young woman who behaves in a brash, laddish way, so lively fits.

clue.text: Fighters shouting, interrupting travellers

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of something else

blocks.note: MiGs are Russian fighter jets
a rant is angry shouting

explanation.surface: Combatants yell and cut in on people passing through.
explanation.definitionFit: Migrants are people on the move from one place to another, so they are travellers.

clue.text: Unions alone must become reformed, but not at the same time

indicators.note: to be reformed is to be remade in a new shape, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Trade unions acting on their own must change their ways, though not all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Simultaneous means happening together, so its negative describes events occurring at different moments.

clue.text: Why courts tape abuse – be careful!

indicators.note: abused material is mistreated and knocked out of its proper shape

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why courts record abuse, then warns the listener to take care.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a warning to proceed cautiously, literally to mind where you put your feet.

clue.text: Trainee clergyman doesn't start up collection

indicators.note: a collection gathers items together in no set order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A trainee vicar fails to begin the church collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't start' tempts you to drop a first letter and 'up' to reverse; in fact those three words are just the letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A student pastor is a minister still in training, a clergyman not yet fully ordained.

clue.text: American pension manager ignoring call for attention in studio

indicators.note: whatever is ignored is left out of the word it belongs to

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a pension is a small continental hotel or boarding house
ho! is a shout to attract notice

explanation.surface: An American running a guest house has no time for anyone seeking attention in his studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Pension here is the European guest house, not a retirement income.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, which is a studio.

clue.text: Drunk legal stood down, getting prohibition notice

indicators.note: someone drunk lurches about, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An inebriated lawyer is stood down and receives a notice of a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase appears on signs barring pets from a place, a typical notice forbidding something.

clue.text: Angry worker grabs one item of food

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one part closes round another

blocks.note: cross means annoyed
I is the Roman numeral one
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A furious employee snatches a single piece of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a flaky crescent-shaped pastry, a specific item eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Copied one that's entering on foot

indicators.note: something entering goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: to ape is to imitate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone imitated a person walking in.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is French, borrowed into English for travelling by foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase a pied means walking, the same as the English expression for going by foot.

clue.text: Tops of yew and fir's fibrous bark (found in the Highlands)

indicators.note: the tops of words in a down-reading sense are their opening letters

blocks.note: first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that yew and fir trees have stringy bark found in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Bark looks like tree bark to match the yew and fir, but it is the dog's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaff is a Scottish dialect verb meaning to bark or yelp like a small dog, hence the Highlands tag.

clue.text: Perhaps Thatcher's advice and negative comment given socialist spin

blocks.note: no is a negative reply
the political left is socialist
a spin is a turn

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher's counsel, offered with a dismissive remark and a socialist slant.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher famously said 'The lady's not for turning'; read as a road sign, her stance becomes a ban on turning, and she was certainly no friend of the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A road sign forbidding a turn to the left playfully matches her refusal to U-turn and her hostility to socialism.

clue.text: Pest from Division welcoming short surprise announcement

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its final letter
to welcome is to take a guest inside, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: an arm of an organisation is a branch or division
'my word!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A pest arrives from an army division, which greets a brief startling news item.
explanation.definitionFit: The armyworm is a moth caterpillar that ravages crops in marching swarms, a notorious agricultural pest.

clue.text: Female's rude shout and short cry after foreign article's not bold enough

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its final letter

blocks.note: un is French for 'a', an article from abroad
her is a female pronoun
oi! is an impolite way to call someone
a call is a cry

explanation.surface: A woman's coarse yell and clipped cry, following a foreign item, lack courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the foreign article first, ahead of the female's pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Unheroical is a rare variant of unheroic, meaning lacking the bravery or boldness of a hero.

clue.text: Kite's treasurer (European) loses annual return and pay

indicators.note: whatever is lost is dropped out of the word it belongs to

blocks.note: Kite is the setter, so 'Kite is' becomes 'I am', shortened
a bursar manages a college's money
AR is the abbreviation for an annual return, the yearly filing a company makes
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: The setter's college treasurer, a European, misses the yearly filing and his salary.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym plus 's stands for 'I'm'. The bracketed European letter is added at the end once the treasurer has lost its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Imburse is an archaic verb meaning to supply with money, hence to pay.

clue.text: See 10 Across
Reviewed a great deal.

indicators.note: re-viewed suggests looking at it again from the other end, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: pots of money means a great deal

explanation.surface: A reviewer says something was assessed at length.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the punctuation itself: the full point at the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed dot ending a sentence is called a full stop, so the mark itself is defined.

clue.text: Muddy son? For a bachelor, quite wet

indicators.note: one thing standing for another means it takes the other's place

blocks.note: boggy ground is muddy
S is the abbreviation for son
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A boy covered in mud; for a single man, that's pretty damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Soggy means soaked through, a state of being thoroughly damp.

clue.text: Rising calls coming from stadiums

blocks.note: a bull market is one where prices are rising
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Mounting shouts are heard from the sports grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Rising is not a reversal signal here; it gives a stock-market term.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullrings are the arenas where bullfights are staged, so they are a kind of stadium.

clue.text: Frost narrated a piece of poetry

indicators.note: something narrated is spoken, so it is judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: The poet Robert Frost recited one of his verses.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the American poet, fitting the poetry, but it is the icy coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme can mean a short verse or poem, as in a nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Charm offensive finally by Belgian city – over investment

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it
to invest is literally to clothe, so one piece is wrapped inside another

blocks.note: last letter
Namur is a city in southern Belgium
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A charm campaign is waged in a Belgian city to win over investors.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to captivate them, the verb sense of charm.

clue.text: US approval for exit perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: an American cry of congratulation
second meaning: a route to follow, of which an exit is one example

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that an exit is only one example of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans say the phrase to praise an achievement; literally it means a route out or onward.

clue.text: Mathematician and doctor at first easily selects second gear

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each word that follows

blocks.note: someone who does sums, read literally
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
first letters
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A mathematician and a doctor, at the start, readily choose the second gear on a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A summer is literally one who sums, a crossword joke rather than a real word for mathematician. Gear means clothing, not a car's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothing, and a light warm-weather frock is an example of it.
